prep.video2: What I did was to listen the video. Then I observed what needed to be done to have a developer mindset and which was to essentially success in the complex and challenging world of game development , by practical strategies  to overcome common obstacles, as technical issues, while maintaining motivation through organization and continuous learning.
prep.video3: What I did was to observed the video about folder structure and what it the best way into doing it. And by the video leaners needs to highlight the important folder structure to improve team efficiency and project management. Then the leader demonstrates how to use a extensions like the Talstra Folder Maker application (showed in the video) that uses custom JSON templates to automate the creation of a essential documentation and project logs.
prep.video4: What I did was to observed the video about documentation and organizing project and what is the best way to do it. Which is by  using a pre-established folder structure. Then the leader demonstrates how to customize a Game Development Document template and explains the function of key project folders like resources, assets, and study area. Also to outline structures to a four-step pipeline to help teams manage their game development process from initial setup through to publishing.
prep.video5: What I did was to observed the video about Intro to Unity. It helps beginners to set up Unity projects and emphasizing proper file management to avoid directory errors. Shows the essentials of the Unity interface and demonstrates basic navigation and character movement controls. The goal is to establish a functional 3D game foundation using a pre-built template, which will be further customized in the future.
prep.video6: What I did was to observed the video about how to import a custom player of your own. And how to do it was by configuring the proper humanoid rig and applying embedded materials. Then the video further explains how to replace a default player mesh by unpacking its prefab and assigning a new avatar to the armature for gameplay integration.
prep.opinion: This pipeline can help future projects/stories. As it helped us understand more about proper organization of folders and files, then help us organize the documentation needed as to tell what we did and need to do in the future, also to have a growth mindset and having it grow so you can think more outside and inside the box for more interesting ideas. With this pipeline it can also help the team acknowledge who is a teammate and tool and if they bring anything to the table or if they are worthy to be in the team.
prep.questions: Out of everything in this pipeline which is more important and why.

huddle.mission: A story I want to see a Minecraft mod a playable goal is to throw a poke-ball at a Minecraft mob
huddle.framework: My team choose P2P for simple fact it will help us use oganized sources and help us with engine setup.
huddle.pipeline:
Unnamed stage
Background · owner Jonathan · 2026-11-11T15:45 to 2026-11-11T16:30 Pacific
inputs/assets · owner mio · 2026-11-11T15:45 to 2026-11-11T16:30 Pacific
build/configure   · owner Isaias · 2026-11-11T15:45 to 2026-11-11T16:30 Pacific
output/scene   · owner Daniel · 2026-11-11T15:45 to 2026-11-11T16:30 Pacific
test+ handoff   · owner Paul · 2026-11-11T15:45 to 2026-11-11T16:30 Pacific
Background-
learn the lore from both source material (Minecraft and Pokemon). Build the world of Minecraft a free roam where the main character is a combination of Ash and Steve.

Inputs/assets- Getting the elements that will be edited and used in the creation of the mod: - Characters, text, animation, 3d models, fonts, audio, etc. Obtaining everything that will be used in order to achieve the results, aka also the things the audience will view.

build/configure-
Put the blocky world together, add an Ash-Steve character so he can walk around, and set up the basic controls for throwing Pokéballs and catching Pokémon as well of building like in a Minecraft world.

Output/scene-
The output is for are mod to allow the player/consumer to be able to throw a poke ball to a Minecraft mob it will also make a custom world when loaded for the player with bits of Pokémon while still looking like Minecraft.

test+handoff-
 We have achieved the results we wanted. We wanted to make a mod pack for the video game Minecraft where we added a poke-ball from Pokemon.
huddle.tech: As a team we have chosen to use unity as the main engine for our game because of our knowledge in C#. We are also going to be using Unity Hub and Package manager. We chose this because based on the lesson videos we saw, we learned a few things about characters and how to create a functioning game, so we have information to get started. Additionally, it is also because we felt that it would be easiest to work with.
huddle.code:
Classes & components
Class | Responsibility | GameObject
pokeballitem | allows the player to throw poke balls | poke ball
pokeballprojectile | handles poke ball throwing and conllions  | projectile
mobcapturesystem | detects and captures minecraft mobs | Minecraft Mobs
pokemonbiome | adds pokemon-theme biomes | biome
pokemonstructures | generaters pokemon-themed buildings and locations | world structures

Variables / properties
Name : type | Value / purpose | Used by
pokeballcount:int | the number of poke ball the player has | poke ball item
targetmob: Enity  | stores the minecraft mob being targeted | pokeballprojectile
capturechance: float  | detemines the chance of capturing mob | mopcapturesystem
worldseed: long | helps generate the custom pokemon-inspired world | pokemonworldgenerator
biometype:string | determines which pokemon-inspired biome generates | pokemon biome

Team check-ins

leader starts the call/texts if we are ready | every Wednesdays | [x]
huddle.reuse: We can reuse the organization patters we are learning/learned from the 6 videos we saw on game development using Unity and Talsta. We can also reuse the story element to build upon what we have and use the skills we have learned to revise our work. We can also continue to further use AI to keep us on track and add new ideas.
huddle.boardNotes: We all had planned to call over Zoom, however, we ran into technical difficulties so we decided to switch to Discord instead. We were on a call for over 2 hours working out our goals and coming up with ideas for our creation. We talked about what elements we want to include in our game, and we also created task boards to help us stay organized. We gave each other different jobs so we can work on separate things, we also discussed how we will be moving forward from this point on as a team.
